lesson.name: Learn The Nimzo Indian Defense
lesson.description: Learn the key ideas for both sides in the strategically rich, Nimzo Indian Defense.

{What precise move did former world champion, Max Euwe find to prevent a pin
on the h4-d8 diagonal?} 11... Ne8 {[%wrong There's a stronger option. Try
again and look for a good knight move.] [%hint Retreat your f6-knight to
prevent any pins.] Good choice! The knight is no longer a target and Black has
the option of meeting f3-f4 with f7-f5 to block the kingside. You may enjoy
checking out the spectacular game, Geller - Euwe, 1953 to learn more about
Black's ideas in the Nimzo Indian.} (11... cxd4 $5 {This is reasonable, but
it's safer to prevent White from pinning with Bg5. How should you do it?}) (
11... Rc8 $5 {This is reasonable, but it's safer to prevent White from pinning
with Bg5. How should you do it?}) (11... h6 $2 12. e5 {White has a dangerous
kingside attack. Try again and look for a way to get your knight out of danger
before White's attack begins.}) (11... Qc7 $2 12. Bg5 {White prepares to
capture on f6 to expose the black king. Try again and look for a way to
prevent Bg5.}) (11... Qc8 $2 12. Bg5 {White prepares to capture on f6 to
expose the black king. Try again and look for a way to prevent Bg5.}) 0-1

{How should Black block the position and prevent White from attacking?} 14...
f5 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try to find it and check the hint if you're
stuck.] [%hint Block the White f-pawn.]} (14... Rc8 $5 {This is playable, but
it's better to restrict White's f-pawn. How should you do it?}) (14... f6 $5 {
This is playable, but it's better to restrict White's f-pawn. How should you
do it?}) (14... cxd4 $5 {This is playable, but it's better to restrict White's
f-pawn. How should you do it?}) (14... g6 $2 15. f5 {White has a powerful
kingside attack. Try to find a stronger move.}) (14... e5 $2 15. Nf5 {White
has a strong attack. Try to find a better move.}) (14... d5 $2 15. cxd5 {
White has a strong attack. Try to find a better move.}) 15. Rae1 {Great start!
How should you further defend the f5 pawn?} g6 {[%wrong There's a better move.
Try to find it and check the hint if you're stuck.] [%hint Defend f5 with
another pawn.] Great job! The blocked pawn on f4 restricts White's dark-squared bishop and the f1 rook. Black went on to win in Botvinnik - Reshevsky
1948. We will check on the game again in the next challenge.} (15... Rd8 $5 {
This is reasonable, but there's a better move. Try to find it.}) (15... Qf7 $2
16. exf5 {White has the initiative. Try to find a better move.}) 0-1

{Black has failed to close the center. What move did GM David Bronstein play
to launch a powerful attack?} 12. f5 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try
again and look for a dangerous pawn break.] [%hint Advance your f-pawn to free
the c1-bishop.]} (12. d5 $2 Na5 {Black is likely to win the c4-pawn and
achieve good counterplay. Try again and look for a stronger pawn move.}) (12.
Rf3 $5 {This is reasonable, but there's a pawn break that's even stronger. Try
to find it.}) (12. e5 $2 g6 {Black prevents the f4-f5 break and keeps a safe
position. Try again and look for a stronger pawn advance.}) 12... e5 {Black
can close the center, but it won't stop the white attack. How should you break
open the black kingside?} 13. f6 {[%wrong Black has a comfortable position.
Try again and look for a stronger pawn sacrifice.] [%hint Sacrifice a pawn to
rip open the black kingside.] Great job! Nxf6 would lose to Bg5 and gxf6 would
lose to Bh6. Bronstein scored a quick win against GM Miguel Najdorf in this
classic game.} (13. d5 $5 {This is a good choice, but Bronstein preferred
another pawn move first. What was his idea?}) *

{White's center looks scary, but Black is just in time to strike back. How
should you fight for center control?} 5... d5 {[%wrong There's a better option.
Try again and look for a precise pawn move.] [%hint Fight for e4 with a pawn.]}
(5... c5 $2 6. e5 {White forces the black knight to retreat and retains an
advantage. Try again and look for a better pawn move.}) (5... d6 $2 6. e5 {
White forces the black knight to retreat and retains an advantage. Try again
and look for a better pawn move.}) (5... Bxc3+ $2 6. bxc3 {White has an
imposing pawn center. Try again and look for a way to fight for the center
with your own pawns.}) 6. e5 {The knight is in danger. Where should it go?} Ne4
{[%wrong White wins material. Try again and look for a precise knight move.] 
[%hint Centralize your knight.] The pin on White's knight ensures Black even
chances in this sharp position.} (6... Bxc3+ $2 7. bxc3 {White has a big
center and the bishop pair. Try again and look for a strong knight move.}) (
6... Nfd7 $2 7. a3 {Black's knight would be much better placed in the center.
Where should it go?}) (6... Ng4 $2 7. h3 {Black's knight would be much
better placed in the center. Where should it go?}) (6... Nh5 $2 7. g4 {The
knight is trapped. Try again and look for a stronger knight move.}) *

[%hint Recapture and attack the white queen.]} (11... Bxd5 $5 {This is
playable but very rare. See if you can find a way to recapture on d5 and make
a threat.}) (11... exd5 $2 12. Bd3 {The c7-pawn is vulnerable and Black's
pieces are somewhat passive. Try to find a more dynamic way to capture on d5.})
12. Bxd8 {Great move! How can you win back the lost material?} Nxc3 {[%wrong

Capture the queen.] Good work! You can take over the white side of this

{How should White save the d8-bishop?} 13. Bh4 {[%wrong There's a better
option. Try again and look for a strong bishop move.] [%hint Retreat your
bishop to safety.]} (13. Bxc7 $2 Nd5 {Black forks c7 and e3 with strong
counterplay. Try again and look for a better bishop move.}) (13. bxc3 $2 Rfxd8
{White loses the bishop pair and any chances for the advantage. Try again and
look for a strong bishop move.}) (13. Be7 $5 {This is playable, but the bishop
won't be safe for long after Re8. Try to find a safer retreat.}) 13... Nd5 {
Good choice! How should you defend the e3-pawn?} 14. Bf2 {[%wrong White is
better off defending the e3-pawn. How should you do it?] [%hint Defend e3 with
a bishop.] Well played! White's bishop pair offers a modest advantage.} (14. e4
$2 Ne3 {Black's knight threatens a fork on c2 and White has a difficult game.
Try again and look for a stronger way to defend the e-pawn.}) (14. Kd2 $2 c5 {
The centralized king is vulnerable to attack. Try again and look for a better
way to defend the e-pawn.}) (14. Ke2 $2 c5 {There's no need to block the
f1-bishop. Try again and look for a better way to defend the e-pawn.}) (14. Kf2
$2 c5 {This is playable, but there's a more useful move to defend e3. Try to
find it.}) *

{Black has just captured on c4, but White is doing well. How should you
prepare to win back material and keep an advantage?} 13. b4 {[%wrong There's a
better move. Try again and look for a useful threat.] [%hint Attack the
a5-knight.]} (13. Rb1 $2 c5 {Black has good counterplay. Try again and look
for a strong threat.}) (13. bxc4 $2 Bxc4 {Black keeps a material advantage. Try
again and look for a useful threat.}) (13. Bxc4 $2 Nxc4 {Black keeps a material
advantage. Try again and look for a useful threat.}) 13... Nb3 {If Black tried
Nc6 or Nb7 then b4-b5 would win material. The knight is in danger of being
trapped on b3 as well. What should White play next?} 14. Rb1 {[%wrong Black
wins material. Try again and look for a way to save your rook.] [%hint Save
your rook and target the b3-knight.] Well played! White prepares b4-b5 to win
back the c4 pawn with a good position.} (14. Ra2 $2 c6 {It's better to use
your rook to target the black knight. How should you do it?}) *

{White's g3 advance was a mistake and White has a strong attack. Try to find a
way for Black to continue the attack.} 11... Ng5 {[%wrong There's a better
option. Try again and look for a strong knight move to threaten checkmate.] 
[%hint Retreat your knight to threaten mate.]} (11... Nxd2 $5 {This is
reasonable, but there's a more aggressive knight move to threaten mate. Try to
find it.}) (11... Qg4 $5 {This is OK, but there's a clever knight move that
gives Black a dangerous attack. Try to find it.}) (11... Qh3 $2 12. Nxe4 {
White wins a pawn. Try again.}) (11... Qh5 $2 12. Nxe4 {White wins a pawn. Try

Black is doing well anyway. How can Black win the game?} Nh3# {[%wrong There's

{Long before he was world champion, Mikhail Botvinnik had a promising attack
out of a Nimzo-Indian style position. How did he expose the white king?} 13...
Bxf3 {[%wrong There's a better attacking idea. Try to find a way to break open
the white kingside.] [%hint Trade pieces to expose the white king.]} 14. Qxa6 {
White preferred to capture on a6 instead of opening the g-file, but Black's
attack is too strong. How should you save the bishop without moving it?} Rg6 {
[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for a strong pin.] [%hint
Pin the g2-pawn.]} (14... Rh6 $5 {This is a good choice but Botvinnik
preferred to pin the g2-pawn. How did he do it?}) (14... Bxg2 $2 15. Kxg2 {
Black doesn't have enough compensation for the lost piece. Try again and look
for a way to pin the g2-pawn.}) 15. g3 {Botvinnik made a small mistake here
and missed the fastest win. How should Black bring more pieces into the attack?
} Qh4 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for the most
aggressive queen move.] [%hint Bring your queen to the h-file.] Well played!
You can finish off the mating attack in the next challenge.} (15... Qg5 $2 16.
Re1 {Botvinnik played this in the game, but there was a faster path to mate.
Try to find a better queen move.}) 0-1
